title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop as it hit the duck. This shows a failure in object detection or motion planning, where the system either did not recognize the duck as an entity requiring avoidance or did not generate a braking response.

Whether the vehicle's perception or decision-making failed, and what training data or test scenarios might have caught this, are not established. A resident claimed the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this after reviewing data. In response, Avride restricted testing in the affected area and began running simulations to prevent similar incidents.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
A self-driving car operated by Avride in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood, triggering significant local backlash. The autonomous vehicle, which had a human safety operator present, did not slow down or stop after hitting the duck that had been nesting in a pot outside a nearby restaurant. Residents became particularly upset because they were familiar with this particular duck, and some have now placed its eggs in an incubator for safekeeping.

Avride confirmed that the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode at the time of the incident. A resident also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this after reviewing vehicle data and simulation replays. In response to the controversy, Avride has restricted its autonomous vehicle testing to exclude certain streets around the lake. The company is now running controlled experiments in simulation to improve the technology and prevent similar situations while maintaining safety performance.
